classification.archetype: Complete a value table, graph a second line and read the simultaneous solution
classification.difficultyReason: Complete a supplied table, plot the second line and interpret its intersection with the supplied line as the simultaneous solution.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Complete the table below for the linear equation $y=2x-1$ and sketch it on the grid provided below where $y=2-x$ is graphed.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
x & -2 & 0 & 2 \\
\hline
y & & & \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

spec.description: Square coordinate grid from -5 to 5 on both axes with minor grid every 1 unit and major grid every 2 units, axes through the origin labelled x and y, tick labels -4, -2, 2, 4. The line y=2-x is drawn and labelled.
spec.mathematics: y=2-x drawn for x from -3 to 5, passing through (0,2), (1,1) and (2,0); label y=2-x near (4.2,-2.2).
spec.answerVisibility: All graph content is permanently visible; the line y=2x-1 is not drawn.

answer.worked:
Substitute each $x$-value into $y=2x-1$:
$$\begin{align*}
x=-2:\ y &= 2(-2)-1 = -5 \\
x=0:\ y &= 2(0)-1 = -1 \\
x=2:\ y &= 2(2)-1 = 3
\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
x & -2 & 0 & 2 \\
\hline
y & -5 & -1 & 3 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$
Plot $(-2,-5)$, $(0,-1)$ and $(2,3)$ and draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: The supplied grid with y=2-x and the sketched line y=2x-1 through the three table points, crossing at (1,1).
spec.mathematics: y=2x-1 through (-2,-5), (0,-1), (2,3); intersection with y=2-x at (1,1).

children.label: b
children.prompt:
From your graph above write down the simultaneous solution of the equations $y=2x-1$ and $y=2-x$.
Point of intersection $(\quad,\quad)$

answer.worked:
The simultaneous solution is the point where the two lines cross, which is $(1,1)$ on the graph.
The point of intersection can be confirmed algebraically:
$$\begin{align*}
2x-1 &= 2-x \\
3x &= 3 \\
x &= 1
\end{align*}$$
Substitute $x=1$:
$$\begin{align*}
y &= 2-1 \\
y &= 1
\end{align*}$$
The simultaneous solution is $(1,1)$.
